clue.text: Put on rack in custodial sentence

definitions.meaning: to put someone on the rack is to pull their limbs out lengthwise
a spell in prison is informally called a ...

explanation.surface: A prisoner is tortured on the rack while serving time in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to pull something out to full length, and slang for a prison term.

clue.text: Anguish concealed by mentors?

indicators.note: concealed by says the answer lies inside the letters of the next word

parts.note: read as two of them, mentor mentor, written side by side

explanation.surface: Suffering hidden behind teachers' guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' licenses reading 'mentors' as MENTOR MENTOR; the answer sits across the join, menTOR MENTor.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is severe physical or mental suffering, a close synonym of anguish.

clue.text: Plant journalists — one of them receives honour

indicators.note: receives says the honour is put inside the journalist

parts.note: an editor is one of the journalists, abbreviated ED
MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: Journalists are placed with troops, and one of them is decorated.
explanation.definitionFit: To embed is to fix firmly in place, as a plant is set in the soil.

clue.text: Composer's strings binding soldiers

indicators.note: binding says the string instruments wrap round the soldiers

parts.note: celli is a plural of cello, a string instrument
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A composer's string section ties up some soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcangelo Corelli was an Italian Baroque violinist and writer of music.

clue.text: Seek answers amid 24 or 25 sheets

parts.note: amid means in, among
a quire is a measure of paper, 24 or 25 sheets

explanation.surface: Someone looks for answers among a sheaf of papers.
explanation.walkthrough: '24 or 25' looks like a cross-reference to other clues, but it is just a count of sheets of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask questions is to seek answers; a plain synonym.

clue.text: Fanatic collecting what's laid up in lump

indicators.note: collecting says the fanatic word holds the other piece

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, a fanatic

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a hen lays an egg

explanation.surface: An enthusiast gathers stored-up goods into a heap.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' signals reading from bottom to top; 'in' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a small lump, especially of gold.

clue.text: In Mexico, druid, dropping boundaries, reconstructed 19, say

definitions.note: the answer at 19 across is an example

indicators.note: reconstructed says the remaining letters are rebuilt in a new order
dropping boundaries removes the outer letters of the run of two words, M and D

explanation.surface: In Mexico a druid's remains are pieced together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping boundaries' trims MEXICODRUID to EXICODRUI, which is then anagrammed. 'In' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk villain at 19 is a wife-killer, so he is an instance of this crime.

clue.text: Neuro-doctor operated on Shakespeare's Globe?

indicators.note: operated on says the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A brain surgeon performed surgery at the famous London theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The Globe looks like the theatre; it means a sphere, in a word Shakespeare used in Sonnet 21.
explanation.definitionFit: Rondure is an old poetic word for a circle or sphere, used by Shakespeare for the round world.

clue.text: Picture of brain spread around, coating new mushroom ring

indicators.note: coating says the spread wraps round the other pieces
around says the spread word is turned back to front

parts.note: marge, short for margarine, is a spread
a cep is a kind of edible mushroom
a halo is a ring of light

explanation.surface: Butter-like spread smeared round a ring of mushrooms makes a picture of a brain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' here is the reversal signal, while 'coating' does the wrapping; the reversed spread is split to enclose the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An encephalogram is a recording or image of the brain's activity or structure.

clue.text: Shakespeare's dog Nipper?

definitions.meaning: Launce's dog in The Two Gentlemen of Verona is named ...
a crustacean with pincers is something that nips

explanation.surface: A dog in Shakespeare that bites people.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the name of Launce's dog in a Shakespeare comedy, and a clawed sea creature that pinches.

clue.text: Force into modest car and get stranded

indicators.note: into says the force letter is pushed inside the car word

parts.note: a runaround is a small, cheap car for local trips
g is the symbol for g-force, the force of gravity

explanation.surface: Someone is squeezed into a little car and ends up stuck somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat runs aground when it strikes the shore or shallows and is left stuck, so the phrase means become stranded.

clue.text: Expected to come back into season, almost like medieval society

indicators.note: into puts the turned word inside the shortened season
almost says the season word loses its last letter

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn

indicators.note: to come back says the word for expected is read backwards

parts.note: something expected is due

explanation.surface: Something anticipated returns in its season, rather like the Middle Ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come back' turns DUE into EUD, and 'almost' trims FALL to FAL; EUD goes into FAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The feudal system of lords, vassals and land tenure organised medieval European society.

clue.text: Non-fliers, holding US wheel-protector back, honourably discharged

indicators.note: holding says the flightless birds contain the other piece

parts.note: emus are flightless birds

indicators.note: back says the American tyre word is read in reverse

parts.note: tire is the American spelling of tyre

explanation.surface: A disjointed image of flightless birds, a tyre and someone leaving service with honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US' belongs with the tyre, pointing to the American spelling, not to the letters US at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus describes someone retired from office with their title kept as an honour.

clue.text: Nameless 23 given high-tension illumination

indicators.note: nameless says the abbreviation for name, N, is removed

parts.note: refers to the answer at 23 across, a bird
HT is the abbreviation for high tension in electrics

explanation.surface: An unnamed bird lit up by a high-voltage source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nameless' drops N (name) from the bird, leaving STARLIG.
explanation.definitionFit: The light shed by the stars is a form of illumination.

clue.text: Allusion to "taste for decapitation"?

indicators.note: for decapitation says the taste word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: a preference is a taste or liking

explanation.surface: A mention of someone's enthusiasm for beheading.
explanation.definitionFit: An allusion is an indirect mention of something, which is what a passing reference is.

clue.text: Man with no time but lots of money?

definitions.text: Man with no time but lots of money?

indicators.note: with no says the letter for time is taken away

parts.note: mister is the title for a man

explanation.surface: A rich man who is too busy to spare a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes a hoarder: he has no time for others but plenty of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinflint hoards wealth and is mean with it, a fitting picture of a rich, ungenerous man.

clue.text: Faux pas boss cut short

indicators.note: cut short says the boss word loses its final letter

parts.note: gaffer is British slang for a boss or foreman

explanation.surface: A blunder made by a boss who was interrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: A faux pas is a social blunder, which is exactly what this word names.

clue.text: The Gaul gets to tear 6 apart

indicators.note: apart says the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: the number six, written out

explanation.surface: The famous Gaul rips the answer at 6 to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like a cross-reference to 6 down but is just the number six.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic-book hero of a Gaulish village resisting Rome is the best-known Gaul of all.

clue.text: 7 squandered stand-in

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 7 down, a man who kills his wife

indicators.note: in says the word for stand goes inside the other word

parts.note: to blue money is British slang for spending it recklessly
to bear is to stand or tolerate

explanation.surface: A bare list of a squandered sum and a stand-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand-in' looks like a substitute, but it splits: 'stand' is the inner word and 'in' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk-tale villain killed his successive wives, the classic example of a wife-murderer.

clue.text: Get into tangle stirring 10 drink

indicators.note: stirring says the letters of ten are mixed up

parts.note: the number ten, written out
wine is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone gets muddled stirring ten drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference but is the number ten; 'stirring' makes ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To entwine is to twist together, so things that entwine become tangled up.

clue.text: Capital inwardly greeting Zambia's rootstock

indicators.note: inwardly says the next pieces go inside the capital

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
hi is a greeting
Z is the international vehicle code for Zambia

explanation.surface: A capital city sends greetings to an African country's plant stem.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhizome is an underground stem that sends out roots and shoots, also called a rootstock.

clue.text: Star teacher is going round university

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir

indicators.note: going round says the word is surrounds the other letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrated teacher is touring a university.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dog Star, brightest in the night sky, is an example of a star.

clue.text: Agog about origin of Liver Bird

indicators.note: about says the agog word goes round the picked letter

parts.note: someone agog is staring wide-eyed

indicators.note: origin of means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An excited crowd gazes at the Liver Bird, the emblem on Liverpool's Royal Liver Building.
explanation.definitionFit: A common speckled songbird, so a straightforward example of a bird.

clue.text: Plough furrow backwards, becoming swollen

indicators.note: backwards says the two words, as they come, are read in reverse

parts.note: to dig is to plough or turn the soil
a rut is a furrow or groove

explanation.surface: A ploughman works a furrow the wrong way and it bulges up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' reverses DIG RUT as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Turgid means distended or bloated, as a swollen limb or overfull river is.

clue.text: Endlessly dressing feathered friend

indicators.note: endlessly says the dressing word loses its last letter

parts.note: robing is putting on robes, dressing

explanation.surface: Dressing up a pet bird over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: A familiar garden songbird with a red breast, a classic example of a bird.

clue.text: Perfume for female Indian of rank holding an animal back

indicators.note: holding says the princess word contains the other pieces

parts.note: a rani is an Indian queen or princess

indicators.note: back says the animal word is read in reverse

parts.note: a pig is an animal

explanation.surface: Scent chosen for a high-born Indian woman who restrains an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses only the animal; 'an' stays forwards, and the pair sits after the princess's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent made from the fragrant flowers of a tropical tree, so a perfume.

clue.text: Kick-start computer

definitions.meaning: to give something a kick with the foot
to load a computer's operating system when switching on

explanation.surface: Giving a computer a jolt to get it going.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: kicking with the foot, and starting up a computer, short for bootstrap.

clue.text: Outlay of former writer extracting Greek character from muse

parts.note: ex means former
a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: extracting says the Greek letter is pulled out of muse

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: The costs of a former writer who has lost a Greek from their inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extracting' removes MU from MUSE, leaving SE.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlay is money spent, which is a cost or charge.

clue.text: Go hither and thither with Shed and 'is missus?

parts.note: Shed is the setter, so from his point of view the word is me
taken as written
his missus is his wife, her, written 'er with the dropped h

explanation.surface: The setter and his wife wander about aimlessly together.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pen name, so Shed = ME. 'is missus is cockney for his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander along a winding course, like a river looping back and forth.
